name: Assess, investigate and treat emergency patients
summary: After triage, patients wait for a treatment space and an emergency physician, who sees them in order of acuity and time waited. The physician takes a history, examines the patient, orders blood tests, imaging and medications, and reassesses when results return before deciding to discharge, consult a specialist, refer to the mental health team or transfer. Most of the elapsed time is waiting: for a space held by admitted patients, for the physician, for results and for repeat tests. Ontario reports time to physician initial assessment and length of stay for every hospital, and the corporation's large site was among the slower ones in 2022/23.

baseline.org_archetype: A three-site Ontario community hospital corporation with about 160,000 ED visits a year, emergency physicians on alternate funding or fee-for-service, computerized order entry and a tracking board.
baseline.notes: Times are a blend weighted toward the large site; the mid-size site was faster to physician assessment in 2022/23 (1.5 h average) and the large site slower (3.3 h).

unit_of_work: one ED visit seen by a physician
trigger: A triaged patient appears in the physician queue on the tracking board.
end_state: The physician has decided the disposition: discharge plan written, consultation requested, crisis team referral made or transfer requested.

volume.seasonality: Follows ED visits: winter respiratory peaks, evening and weekend peaks for low-acuity patients without primary care access.

resources.name: Emergency treatment spaces, large site (stretchers, chairs and resuscitation bays)

steps.name: Reassess the waiting patient
steps.description: While the patient waits for a space or a physician, the triage nurse checks the waiting room list against the reassessment interval for each CTAS level, repeats vital signs for patients waiting longest and asks whether symptoms have changed.

evidence.note: Author's general knowledge of CTAS reassessment in waiting rooms; the CTAS 2016 revision page opened did not state intervals.

steps.name: Re-triage a patient who got worse
steps.description: The nurse raises the CTAS level in the system, tells the charge nurse and moves the patient up the list for the next stretcher, starting any directive orders that now apply.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Wait for a treatment space
steps.description: The charge nurse brings the next patient from the waiting room when a stretcher or chair and a nurse come free, choosing by CTAS level and time waited. Admitted patients waiting for inpatient beds hold many ED stretchers, so this wait grows when the hospital is full.

evidence.note: OAG 2023: admitted patients waited on average 13 hours for an inpatient bed in 2022/23 (Mississauga Halton 10.8 hours in 2021/22), occupying ED space; the wait range is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Do the primary nursing assessment
steps.description: The primary nurse checks the identity band, takes a full set of vital signs, does a focused assessment for the complaint, starts a cardiac monitor or IV if needed and documents in the nursing record. The treatment space stays occupied by this patient until they leave.

next.condition: patient violent or at risk of harm

evidence.note: Nurse assessment is a step in the OAG 2023 patient flow (Figure 3); minutes are the author's estimate. Space occupancy runs to disposition (about 2-8 hours).

steps.name: Physician initial assessment
steps.description: The emergency physician picks the next patient from the tracking board by CTAS level and wait, reads the triage note and any directive results, takes a history and examines the patient, and forms a working diagnosis. This is the time-to-physician the province reports.

error.defect_description: Missed or wrong working diagnosis, often found on reassessment or a return visit.

control.basis: Diagnosis and orders by a physician holding emergency privileges (Regulated Health Professions Act controlled acts; hospital medical staff by-laws)

evidence.note: OAG 2023: average 118 minutes and 90th percentile 257 minutes from triage to physician initial assessment in Ontario in 2022/23; 2022/23 averages of 1.5 h (mid-size site), 2.5 h (small site) and 3.3 h (large site) for the corporation's hospitals (Appendix 3). Touch minutes are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Enter test and medication orders
steps.description: The physician enters laboratory, imaging and medication orders in the hospital system, choosing from ED order sets for chest pain, abdominal pain or sepsis, and flags urgent ones to the nurse.

evidence.note: Author's general knowledge of computerized order entry in Ontario hospitals.

steps.name: Carry out orders
steps.description: The nurse starts an IV, draws and labels blood, sends specimens to the laboratory by pneumatic tube, takes medications from the automated dispensing cabinet and gives them, and books the patient for imaging.

error.defect_description: Specimen mislabelled or haemolysed and has to be redrawn.

control.basis: Two patient identifiers at specimen collection and medication administration (hospital policy; Accreditation Canada required organizational practice)

evidence.note: Author's estimate of nursing work and imaging shares; OAG 2023 lists blood work, ultrasound and CT as typical diagnostic steps.

steps.name: Take the patient to X-ray
steps.description: A patient care assistant or porter takes the patient to the emergency X-ray room and back once imaging calls for them, waiting while the technologist does the films.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Take the patient to CT or ultrasound
steps.description: A patient care assistant, with a nurse for monitored patients, takes the patient to CT or ultrasound once the scanner is free, waits during the scan and brings the patient back.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; CT scanner count from the organisation file.

steps.name: Results come back
steps.description: Laboratory results flow from the laboratory system into the hospital record and the radiologist's report appears after dictation; the tracking board shows a results-ready flag. No one works on the case while it waits.

evidence.note: OAG 2023 notes waiting for blood tests or imaging results as unavoidable ED time; durations are the author's estimate of community-hospital turnaround.

steps.name: Reassess with results
steps.description: When the physician gets to the patient again, they read the results and images, re-examine the patient and decide whether the diagnosis is settled or more time, treatment or tests are needed.

next.condition: needs observation, repeat tests or more treatment

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Observe and treat over time
steps.description: The nurse gives further fluids, analgesia or nebulizers, repeats vital signs and draws the repeat troponin or other timed test, then flags the physician when the patient is ready for review. Stable patients in the sub-acute zone are often cared for by a practical nurse.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; repeat cardiac markers are usually timed hours after the first.

steps.name: Decide the disposition
steps.description: The physician decides whether the patient can go home, needs a specialist's opinion or admission, needs the mental health crisis team, or must be transferred to another hospital, and tells the patient and nurse.

evidence.note: OAG 2023: about 12% of Ontario ED visits were admitted in 2022/23. Shares follow the organisation file's process volumes (consults 1,900, crisis 450, transfers 60 of 12,600 a month).

steps.name: Write the discharge plan
steps.description: The physician writes the diagnosis, prescriptions and follow-up (family doctor, fracture clinic, return if worse) and the discharge instructions the nurse will go through with the patient.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Complete the physician record
steps.description: The physician finishes the emergency record, signs orders and records the diagnosis used for the CIHI ambulatory care record and for OHIP or alternate-funding billing.

control.basis: Public Hospitals Act record requirements and CIHI NACRS reporting of emergency visits

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Request a specialist consultation
steps.description: The physician decides a specialist must see or admit the patient and asks the unit clerk to page the on-call physician for that service, noting the question to be answered.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; consultation is the route to admission in Ontario community hospitals.

steps.name: Refer to the mental health crisis team
steps.description: For a patient in mental health crisis, the physician completes a risk assessment, decides whether to hold the patient under a Mental Health Act form and refers to the crisis clinician and psychiatrist on call.

control.basis: Ontario Mental Health Act (application for psychiatric assessment by a physician)

evidence.note: Author's general knowledge of Ontario ED mental health pathways; share from the organisation file's crisis volume.

steps.name: Arrange a transfer to another hospital
steps.description: For a patient needing a service the site lacks, the physician calls CritiCall Ontario, presents the case to the accepting physician at the receiving hospital and writes the transfer note.

evidence.note: Author's general knowledge of CritiCall referrals; minutes estimated.

steps.name: Resuscitate a critically ill patient
steps.description: The emergency physician leads the resuscitation in the resuscitation bay: airway, breathing and circulation, drugs and procedures, while ordering urgent tests and calling ICU or other services.

control.basis: Physician-led resuscitation under hospital medical staff by-laws

evidence.note: CTAS level 1 patients are seen immediately (ctas2016); OAG 2023 reports CTAS 1 patients typically saw a physician within 30 minutes. Duration is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Nursing team runs the resuscitation
steps.description: Three nurses work alongside the physician: one records, one gives drugs and fluids, one does compressions, monitoring and procedures, with a respiratory therapist for airway support.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of resuscitation team size.

steps.name: Call security for a violent patient
steps.description: The charge nurse calls a code white, security officers attend, and staff use de-escalation and, only if needed, physical or chemical restraint on a physician's order with documented monitoring.

control.basis: Ontario Patient Restraints Minimization Act and hospital least-restraint policy

evidence.note: Author's estimate; share from the organisation file's security response volume.

steps.name: Approve over-capacity measures
steps.description: The patient care manager (the administrator on call at night) approves opening over-capacity stretchers, placing admitted patients in hallways or on inpatient units early, and calling in extra staff.

evidence.note: OAG 2023 describes hallway care and admitted patients waiting in the ED; escalation practice and frequency are the author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Repeat testing and observation
exceptions.description: Chest pain and similar patients wait hours for a repeat timed test before a decision.

exceptions.name: Resuscitation
exceptions.description: Critically ill patients go straight to the resuscitation bay with a physician-led team.

exceptions.name: Department over capacity
exceptions.description: No spaces are free and the manager approves surge measures.

exceptions.name: Violent or high-risk behaviour
exceptions.description: Security is called and restraint may be used.

evidence.note: OAG 2023 section 4.2.1 and Figure 10.

evidence.note: OAG 2023 Appendix 3 (Halton Healthcare: Milton District 1.5, Georgetown 2.5, Oakville-Trafalgar Memorial 3.3).

pain_points.description: Admitted patients waiting for inpatient beds occupy ED stretchers, so new patients wait in the waiting room for a space.

evidence.note: OAG 2023 section 4.2.4: average 13-hour wait for an inpatient bed in 2022/23, 21.3 hours in Mississauga Halton.

pain_points.description: Time to physician initial assessment is long and varies widely between hospitals, and the large site was among the slower ones.

evidence.note: OAG 2023 Appendix 3 and section 4.2.1.

pain_points.description: Waiting for laboratory and imaging results, and for timed repeat tests, makes up much of the visit.

evidence.note: OAG 2023 calls waiting for blood tests or imaging results unavoidable ED time and notes inconsistent use of medical directives to start them earlier.

pain_points.description: Low-acuity patients without timely primary care use the ED, adding to physician queues in evenings and weekends.

evidence.note: OAG 2023: CTAS 4 and 5 were about 23% of visits in 2022/23.

assumptions: The simulated median (about 4.8 hours) is about 1.25 times the benchmark built from provincial averages; the corporation's large site averaged 3.3 hours to physician assessment in 2022/23 against 2.0 hours for Ontario, so a longer median than the provincial anchor is expected.

Laboratory results, imaging reports and consult notes are inputs that return within a case, not separate case triggers, so they are listed under interfaces.inputs rather than triggered_by (the organisation file lists them as triggers).
The process ends at the disposition decision; discharge teaching, consultation and boarding are separate workflows, so simulated cycle time is shorter than the provincial length-of-stay measures.
Patients who leave without being seen (about 3%) leave during the waits before s05 and are excluded from the volume, as in the organisation file.
Specimen collection, imaging exams and pharmacy verification are separate processes; here only the ED staff's part and the wait are modelled.
ED treatment space use is booked to the large site's spaces (ed_spaces_otmh) as the representative site; occupancy at s04 covers the whole visit to disposition.
Stated nursing FTE counts only the share of primary nursing on assessment and orders; total ED nursing is much larger because of ongoing care and admitted patients boarding in the ED.
The 2019-2022 period mixes pre-pandemic crowding, the 2020/21 drop in visits and the 2021-2022 staffing shortages; times are a blend, with the 2022/23 provincial figures as the upper anchor.
